entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Pharnaces II of Pontus was the king of the Bosporan Kingdom and Kingdom of Pontus until his death. He was a monarch of Persian and Greek ancestry. He was the youngest child born to King Mithridates VI of Pontus from his first wife, his sister Queen Laodice. He was born and raised in the Kingdom of Pontus and was the namesake of his late double great grandfather Pharnaces I of Pontus. After his father was defeated by the Romans in the Third Mithridatic War and died in 63 BC, the Romans annexed the western part of Pontus, merged it with the former Kingdom of Bithynia and formed the Roman province of Bithynia and Pontus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Pharnaces II of Pontus played a significant role in shaping regional politics after his father's defeat by the Romans. His kingdom was annexed by Rome and merged with Bithynia, leading to the formation of the Roman province of Bithynia and Pontus.
